name: The priests who despised the Name
charge: Offering polluted bread and blemished beasts; being partial in the law
summary: After the return, the priests offered the blind, the lame, and the sick on the altar and said the table of the Lord was contemptible and its service a weariness. Offer it now unto thy governor, Malachi says; will he be pleased with thee? They also departed out of the way and caused many to stumble at the law.
offense: The priests despised the Lord's name by bringing polluted offerings and treating His table as contemptible. They offered the blind, lame, and sick, though such a gift would not please their governor. Their conduct withheld from the great King the honor they understood how to show to earthly authority (Malachi 1:6-14).
judgment: I will curse your blessings; yea, I have cursed them already. I will spread dung upon your faces, even the dung of your solemn feasts. Therefore have I also made you contemptible and base before all the people, according as ye have been partial in the law.

entries.commentary: The Levitical priesthood was established in Aaron and his sons. Certain things were consecrated that could not be touched by the rest of Israel, and a priest with his uncleanness upon him could not go unto the holy things, lest that soul be cut off from the presence of the Most High. Aaron was consecrated and anointed to minister in the priest's office, and his sons were clothed and anointed as their father, an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.

A man of the seed of Aaron that was a leper, had a running issue, or touched any unclean thing could not eat of the holy things until he was clean: he washed his flesh with water, and when the sun was down he was clean and could afterward eat. That which dieth of itself, or is torn with beasts, he shall not eat to defile himself therewith. That same law elsewhere says to give such a thing unto the stranger or sell it to an alien, for thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: these laws were given to Israel alone, and the other nations may eat those things because they are not the holy people. There is no equality in that.

No stranger may eat of the holy thing, neither a sojourner of the priest nor an hired servant. But the soul the priest buys with his money, and he that is born in his house, they eat of his meat, because they are joined to the priest's household. The priest's daughter married unto a stranger may not eat of the offering of the holy things; but if she is a widow or divorced and has no child, and is returned unto her father's house as in her youth, she eats of her father's meat, because she returns to her father's covering. A woman was commonly under her father's covering until she came under a husband's. The independent woman was not birthed from the Bible; she was birthed from Babylon. He that eats of the holy thing unwittingly adds the fifth part unto it and gives it to the priest with the holy thing; the priests must not suffer the children of Israel to bear the iniquity of trespass when they eat their holy things.

Whatever offering is brought for a vow or a freewill offering must be a male without blemish, of the beeves, of the sheep, or of the goats. Beeves goes to the ox and that family, the oxen and bulls. Blind, broken, maimed, or having a wen, or scurvy, or scabbed, shall not be offered unto the Lord. Scurvy is just having scratches; these offerings could have no scratches and no bruises, nothing bruised or crushed or broken or cut. Neither from a stranger's hand shall ye offer the bread of your God of any of these, because their corruption is in them and blemishes be in them; they shall not be accepted for you.

When a bullock or a sheep or a goat is brought forth, it shall be seven days under the dam. The dam is that animal's mother; the young must stay under its mother seven days, and from the eighth day it is accepted for an offering. Whether it be cow or ewe, ye shall not kill it and her young both in one day. And the sacrifice of thanksgiving is eaten the same day; none of it is left until the morrow.

Therefore shall ye keep my commandments and do them: neither shall ye profane my holy name, but I will be hallowed among the children of Israel. I am the Lord which brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God. The Most High brought Israel out of the land of Egypt to be their God; that is the foundation the commandments stand on.

At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release: every creditor that lendeth ought unto his neighbour shall release it, and shall not exact it of his neighbour or of his brother, because it is called the Lord's release. Of a foreigner thou mayest exact it again, but that which is thine with thy brother thine hand shall release. The seven year release stands on the sabbath of the land already given in [Leviticus 25](/bible/leviticus/25).

If thou carefully hearken unto the voice of the Most High to observe all these commandments, thou shalt lend unto many nations but thou shalt not borrow, and thou shalt reign over many nations but they shall not reign over thee. This is the blessing that was to come upon us. Since we broke the commandments of the Most High, the other nations lend to us and we borrow from them; we go to them for loans and everything else.

If there be among you a poor man of one of thy brethren, thou shalt not harden thine heart nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother. It is a commandment to us to help our brothers: open thine hand wide unto him and lend him sufficient for his need, in that which he wanteth.

Beware that there be not a thought in thy wicked heart saying, The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand, and thine eye be evil against thy poor brother and thou givest him nought; if he cry unto the Lord against thee, it is sin unto thee. Give him surely, and let not thine heart be grieved when thou givest, for because of this thing the Most High shall bless thee in all thy works. Notice that Esau had this Bible, these commandments and these laws, yet worked us to death for over four hundred years, and when they released us we did not go out with anything. They had these laws written before them and did not do them. The poor shall never cease out of the land; Christ said the same, that the poor are always going to be among us. That is why no campaign can fight poverty out of existence: Christ said it will always be among us.

If thy brother, an Hebrew man or an Hebrew woman, be sold unto thee and serve thee six years, then in the seventh year thou shalt let him go free, and thou shalt not let him go away empty. When people say slavery was taking place in Africa among us, it was not slavery like we suffered: it was people among us that fell poor and sold themselves to their brothers, the very case this law and [Leviticus 25](/bible/leviticus/25) govern. Thou shalt furnish him liberally out of thy flock, out of thy floor, and out of thy winepress; he must leave blessed, with some of the flock, the corn, and the wine. He cannot go out poor the way he came in; that shows you the Most High is a good God. The reason given is memory: remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt, and the Lord thy God redeemed thee.

If the servant say, I will not go away from thee, because he loveth thee and thine house and is well with thee, then thou shalt take an aul and thrust it through his ear unto the door, and he shall be thy servant for ever; likewise unto thy maidservant. It shall not seem hard unto thee when thou sendest him away free, for he hath been worth a double hired servant to thee in serving thee six years. A double hired servant: reading this makes you think about slavery and how many years they had us. We were double hired servants unto them, and we still serve them even to this day.

All the firstling males of thy herd and of thy flock thou shalt sanctify unto the Most High: thou shalt do no work with the firstling of thy bullock, nor shear the firstling of thy sheep. The firstlings were to do no work at all; they were to be sacrificed to the Most High, and thou shalt eat it before the Lord thy God year by year in the place which the Lord shall choose. If there be any blemish therein, as if it be lame or blind, thou shalt not sacrifice it unto the Lord thy God; thou shalt eat it within thy gates, the unclean and the clean person alike, as the roebuck and as the hart. Only thou shalt not eat the blood thereof; thou shalt pour it upon the ground as water.

verses.text: A son honoureth his father, and a servant his master: if then I be a father, where is mine honour? and if I be a master, where is my fear? saith the Lord of hosts unto you, O priests, that despise my name. And ye say, Wherein have we despised thy name?
Ye offer polluted bread upon mine altar; and ye say, Wherein have we polluted thee? In that ye say, The table of the Lord is contemptible.

And if ye offer the blind for sacrifice, is it not evil? and if ye offer the lame and sick, is it not evil? offer it now unto thy governor; will he be pleased with thee, or accept thy person? saith the Lord of hosts.
But ye have profaned it, in that ye say, The table of the Lord is polluted; and the fruit thereof, even his meat, is contemptible.

Ye said also, Behold, what a weariness is it! and ye have snuffed at it, saith the Lord of hosts; and ye brought that which was torn, and the lame, and the sick; thus ye brought an offering: should I accept this of your hand? saith the Lord.

But cursed be the deceiver, which hath in his flock a male, and voweth, and sacrificeth unto the Lord a corrupt thing: for I am a great King, saith the Lord of hosts, and my name is dreadful among the heathen.
And now, O ye priests, this commandment is for you.

If ye will not hear, and if ye will not lay it to heart, to give glory unto my name, saith the Lord of hosts, I will even send a curse upon you, and I will curse your blessings: yea, I have cursed them already, because ye do not lay it to heart.
Behold, I will corrupt your seed, and spread dung upon your faces, even the dung of your solemn feasts; and one shall take you away with it.
For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.
But ye are departed out of the way; ye have caused many to stumble at the law; ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi, saith the Lord of hosts.
Therefore have I also made you contemptible and base before all the people, according as ye have not kept my ways, but have been partial in the law.
But whatsoever hath a blemish, that shall ye not offer: for it shall not be acceptable for you.

And whosoever offereth a sacrifice of peace offerings unto the Lord to accomplish his vow, or a freewill offering in beeves or sheep, it shall be perfect to be accepted; there shall be no blemish therein.
Blind, or broken, or maimed, or having a wen, or scurvy, or scabbed, ye shall not offer these unto the Lord, nor make an offering by fire of them upon the altar unto the Lord.
And if there be any blemish therein, as if it be lame, or blind, or have any ill blemish, thou shalt not sacrifice it unto the Lord thy God.

lawsResolved.text: Ministers are not to profane the name of their God.
A priest is to teach the people the difference between holy and profane and to discern between unclean and clean.
Ministers are to teach the people all the laws and statutes of God.
You are not to be partial towards anyone or a respecter of persons in exacting justice, whether they be poor or rich, small or great.
We are to honor God by bringing the choice first fruits of our land into the house of God, so He may bring prosperity to us.
Lying pastors and those that withhold the truth of God's word are cursed for causing national apostasy.
